title: Space Tourism Awareness
desc: Understand what suborbital and orbital tourism are, the risks, cost, rules and careers, and how to read claims.
task: Produce a two-page fact sheet on space tourism with flight types, risks, costs, environmental impact and careers.
condition: A computer, public information, two peers and a mentor.
standard: Facts sourced and dated; risks stated; claims checked; peers rate Meets or better.
modules: A common line is 100 km up.
Suborbital goes up and falls back.
A short flight gives a few minutes of weightlessness.
Costs are in the hundreds of thousands and above.
A seat costs more than a lifetime of savings for most.
Soot and gases in high air.
A spaceport employs hundreds in ground roles.
rubric: Every claim linked to a dated record and checked by a peer
Checked, dated and explained to others
ladder: What counts as space

L1: learner can say what space is. Focus module: What counts as space (Understand, 2 h). The edge of space. Key points: A common line is 100 km up. Suborbital goes up and falls back. Orbital circles Earth.

Teach: open with the worked example. A short flight gives a few minutes of weightlessness. Then set the activity: Explain the difference. Mark against the standard: Peer understands. Check at this level: Space line? Model answer: About 100 km. Define.
Flight types

L2: learner knows flight types. Focus module: Flight types (Understand, 2 h). Rocket, balloon, plane. Key points: Rocket planes, capsules, high balloons. Time, altitude and experience vary. Training is needed.

Teach: open with the worked example. Balloon flights reach about 30 km. Then set the activity: Compare types. Mark against the standard: Table complete. Check at this level: Suborbital? Model answer: Up and back without orbit. Types.
Safety and health

L3: learner can read a profile. Focus module: Safety and health (Evaluate, 2 h). Risk is real. Key points: Acceleration, vibration, radiation, emergencies. Medical checks and training. Incident history is public.

Teach: open with the worked example. Passengers train for high G. Then set the activity: List risks. Mark against the standard: Each risk has a control. Check at this level: Name a risk. Model answer: High G or radiation. Profile.
Cost and access
L4: learner can compare costs. Focus module: Cost and access (Analyse, 2 h). Very expensive today. Key points: Costs are in the hundreds of thousands and above. Price may fall. Access is unequal.

Teach: open with the worked example. A seat costs more than a lifetime of savings for most. Then set the activity: Discuss fairness. Mark against the standard: Fair views. Check at this level: Cost? Model answer: Very high today. Costs.
Environment
L5: learner can review safety. Focus module: Environment (Analyse, 2 h). Rockets emit. Key points: Soot and gases in high air. Launch frequency matters. Fuel type changes impacts.

Teach: open with the worked example. Per passenger emissions are high. Then set the activity: Check a claim. Mark against the standard: Source dated. Check at this level: Environmental issue? Model answer: Emissions in high air. Safety.
Careers and ground services

L6: learner can coordinate guest services. Focus module: Careers and ground services (Understand, 2 h). Not just pilots. Key points: Engineers, medics, trainers, guides, safety. Hospitality and data roles. Local spaceports.

Teach: open with the worked example. A spaceport employs hundreds in ground roles. Then set the activity: List ten roles. Mark against the standard: Roles correct. Check at this level: Rule? Model answer: Licence and informed consent. Team.
Fact sheet
L7: learner can audit a sheet. Focus module: Fact sheet (Create, 2 h). Balanced writing. Key points: Plain language. State limits. Test with a reader.

Teach: open with the worked example. Reader repeats three facts. Then set the activity: Finish. Mark against the standard: Reader can repeat. Check at this level: Ground roles? Model answer: Engineers, medics, trainers. Peer audit.
